links.outcome: Recognition and appropriate triage of emergent cases by GPT-3
links.effect: GPT-3 triaged 70% correct (34/48) versus 91% for physicians; GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.
links.quote: For triage error analysis, GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.

links.outcome: GPT-3 diagnostic and triage accuracy compared with physicians and laypeople on same vignettes
links.effect: Diagnosis top-3: GPT-3 88% vs lay 54% (p<0.0001) vs physicians 96% (p=0.012). Triage: GPT-3 70% vs lay 74% (p=0.60) vs physicians 91% (p<0.0001).
links.quote: GPT-3 triaged 70% correct (34/48, 57-82) versus 74% (3706/5000, 73-75; p=0.60) for lay individuals and 91% (608/666, 89-93%; p<0.0001) for physicians.

links.outcome: Calibration of GPT-3 confidence in diagnosis and triage (Brier score)
links.effect: Confidence reasonably well calibrated: Brier score 0.18 for diagnosis and 0.22 for triage.
links.quote: As measured by the Brier score, GPT-3 confidence in its top prediction was reasonably well calibrated for diagnosis (Brier score=0·18) and triage (Brier score=0·22).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic and triage accuracy and calibration of GPT-3 against physicians and laypeople using synthetic clinical vignettes, but it does not test a specific implementation guardrail or deployment practice.
